card-prompt.purpose: Primary retrieval question in study column; SwiftUI .largeTitle

card-secondary.purpose: Supporting card content beneath the answer; SwiftUI .title2

ui-display.purpose: The one number a pane exists to deliver, today the scope home due headline; SwiftUI .title2 bold with monospaced digits. Bold rather than larger, because sizes above this belong to the card.

ui-title.purpose: Pane titles and sheet headlines; SwiftUI .title2 semibold. Emphasis here is weight and space, never card sizes.

ui-row-title.purpose: Compact sidebar destination or deck name; SwiftUI .body

ui-row-meta.purpose: Compact trailing actionable status such as due count; SwiftUI .caption

motion.name: reveal-crossfade
motion.purpose: Answer reveal in study view; disabled when Reduce Motion is on — use instant cut.

motion.name: grade-submit
motion.purpose: No animation between cards; swap content immediately to preserve study flow.

platformNotes.macOS14: Semantic system colors; standard NavigationSplitView materials.
platformNotes.macOS26: Optional Liquid Glass on sidebar and toolbar only; study content stays opaque.
platformNotes.iOSFuture: Stack navigation; bottom-fixed grade bar; 44pt touch targets.

components.description: Centered non-scrolling adaptive card stage, max 600pt. Named Focus, Split, Media Aside, Media Hero, and Action Stage compositions own responsive geometry; measured overflow opens a separate full-content sheet.

components.name: Scope Home Summary
components.description: Default detail pane for a sidebar scope: the due count as a bold display headline, one prominent Study action, a neutral typographic card-state breakdown under a quiet group label, and a secondary link into browse mode. The scope name lives in the window title, not above the headline — the headline has nothing to compete with, and everything below it is quieter than a section heading. No card type sizes, no colored stat pills, no progress rings.

narrative.overview: NeoAnki2 should feel like a well-lit desk: one open page (the card), a tidy shelf of decks to the side, and almost nothing else competing for attention. Selecting a scope answers what to study now; enumerating items is a deliberate browse mode you ask for. Platform-native restraint and content-forward layout. The card is the only hero per screen.
keyCharacteristics: Content-first: the selected Focus, Split, Media Aside, Media Hero, or Action Stage composition dominates the detail pane
The active Study Stage does not scroll; its action/grading footer is fixed. Measured overflow opens a separate full-content sheet.
Presets own responsive geometry. Authored data selects named regions and semantic purposes but never supplies arbitrary layout or markup.
Mac-native: NavigationSplitView, menus, keyboard shortcuts, tooltips
Semantically colored: SwiftUI system colors, not hard-coded grays
Restrained accent: tint appears on no more than two primary actions per screen
Tonal depth: sidebar vs detail via system surfaces, not custom shadows
No gamification visuals: no streak flames, progress rings, or confetti

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The system accent appears only on primary forward actions (Study, Show Answer, Done on completion, and an empty state's single call to action). Grade buttons, list rows, browse chrome, and toolbars stay neutral bordered styles.

rules.name: The No Gamification Palette Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce streak orange, achievement gold, or chart rainbow colors. Progress is text (8 cards remaining), not rings or bars. The count includes each unresolved card once, so grading Again keeps it stable instead of moving a denominator.

rules.name: The Card Type Scale Rule
rules.body: Only card prompt uses .largeTitle; only card answer uses .title. UI chrome never borrows card sizes. Chrome that must lead a pane reaches for uiDisplay's weight and the space around it rather than asking for an exception.

rules.name: The Dynamic Type Rule
rules.body: Use semantic SwiftUI text styles via DesignSystem.Typography — never hard-coded point sizes in production views.

rules.name: The Split-First Rule
rules.body: Study never returns to a sheet modal on Mac. Detail pane owns the session.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Card text lives in a centered column capped at 600pt. Wide windows add margin, not longer line lengths. Dense tables in browse mode take the full detail width.

rules.name: The Study-Forward Default Rule
rules.body: The detail pane's default branch answers what to do now. A bare list of everything is never the landing state for a scope.

rules.name: The No Answers by Default Rule
rules.body: No library surface reveals an item's answer without an explicit request. Browse mode ships the Answer column hidden; row subtitles never carry it. The reveal lives in the menu bar with a shortcut and persists.

rules.name: The Flat Study Stage Rule
rules.body: The study card is not a Card component with shadow. It is text on the desk — divider and typography hierarchy only.

rules.name: The Platform Shape Rule
rules.body: If SwiftUI or AppKit provides the control, use its default geometry. Custom radii are only for media containers.

dos: Do use semantic SwiftUI colors (.primary, .secondary, .tertiary, and .red for errors with icons).
Do keep one primary action visible per study phase (Show Answer or grade row, never both prominent).
Do expose keyboard paths (Space/Return, 1–4, Command-Shift-S) and document them in Grade Help.
Do test Light, Dark, and Increased Contrast before shipping UI changes.
Do adopt Liquid Glass on sidebar/toolbar when targeting macOS 26, with opaque study content.
donts: Don't gamify with streaks, XP, leaderboards, celebratory animations, or progress rings.
Don't use hard-coded #888 grays; they break Dark Mode.
Don't put custom shadows, gradients, or glass on card content.
Don't use display serifs, condensed fonts, or flashcard-app-cute illustration styles.
Don't copy Anki's dense toolbar/grid aesthetic or Quizlet's bright game UI.
Don't show scheduling statistics during active review; the scope home is where they belong before a session.
Don't reveal an answer anywhere in the library without being asked.
